$comment: Authored by hand, once. The token sets are generated into `generated/` from tokens.ts by `npm run grammar` — never edit the generated file. What lives here is the part that does not change when the language grows a keyword: the repository rules, the begin/end pairs, and the scope names.
name: DriftScript

declaration.$comment: A name in a declaring position, so `data Door` highlights `Door` as a type rather than as a variable. The keyword itself is matched by the generated keyword rule; this only names what follows it. Order is load-bearing twice over: TextMate takes the first match, so a rule with a clause must precede the plain form it extends — `data Wolf : Dog` before `data`, and `component Transform from host` before `component`. The entity-form rules are appended rather than interleaved because no earlier rule can match their heads, and `scripts/grammar.test.mjs` reads the first three by position.

patterns.$comment: `data Wolf : Dog` — the base is a type too. Without this the record reads as declared and its base as an ordinary word, which is the one part of the line a reader is looking for.

`component Transform from host` — the assertion direction. It must precede the plain `component` rule, because TextMate takes the first match and the plain rule would consume the head and leave `from host` unhighlighted, which is the one part of that line that says the declaration creates nothing.
A system is named like a function rather than like a type: it is a body that runs, and the schedule addresses it by that name.
